Attachment theory suggests that infants begin to show clear attachment behaviors around 6–8 months of age, with stranger anxiety typically emerging around 8–9 months.  
A child raised in a neglectful environment may have an insecure attachment style, making them more likely to seek comfort from unfamiliar adults when distressed.  
Option (C) describes an 8-month-old male infant with a neglectful single caregiver — this child is old enough to have formed attachments but may be more inclined to attach to an unfamiliar adult due to inconsistent caregiving.  

Final answer: (C)
